summary: Rach2's KVM run by Debian's QEMU on the x86-64 GNU root: the Debian guest of tests/kvm/guests booted to its token by tests/kvm/kvm-boot.sh, and kvm-unit-tests and Linux's KVM selftests run by tests/kvm/corpus.sh as tests/kvm/unit-tests.list and selftests.list say, on the max-svm and host-svm processor profiles; the scenario is tests/cases/machine/kvm_scenario.c

cases.behavior: A small real-mode guest runs under SVM: nested page faults, CPUID, CR0, RDMSR, port I/O and HLT, and a memory slot whose frame is replaced

execution.privileges: the runner runs as root in the guest, which opens /dev/kvm and mounts the data disk
execution.cleanup: libetude-case stops the machine and removes the overlay, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot an overlay of the GNU system's disk on AHCI with rach2.root=ext2 and no display, wait for the root and the login prompt, log in as root at the console and open the framed guest channel

run svm-entry, whose real-mode guest reads a slot, executes intercepted instructions and reads a replacement frame

assertions.checks: svm-entry exits 0 and prints SVMENTRY OK after every guest exits through OUT and HLT

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

cases.behavior: An ordinary user's random ioctls on /dev/kvm, a VM with a memory slot and a vCPU, for 20000 calls of seed 1, end with no fault the kernel records and every live KVM count back to its value before

execution.privileges: the runner starts as root in the guest, which mounts the data disk; drmfuzz's child drops to uid and gid 65534 before it opens /dev/kvm
execution.cleanup: libetude-case stops the machine and removes the overlay, which it keeps after a failure
